references.text: God's Spirit came upon Zechariah, the son of the priest Jehoiada, and he stood before the people and said that they had forsaken the Lord. They conspired against him and stoned him in the courtyard of the Lord's house – an example of Jerusalem killing the prophets and stoning those sent to the city ([ref:2 Chr 24:21|2 Chronicles 24:21]).

Nehemiah describes Israel's repeated rebellion: they killed the prophets who urged them to turn back to the Lord. This confirms Jesus' lament over Jerusalem's habit of killing the prophets sent to them ([ref:Neh 9:26|Nehemiah 9:26]).
The prophet Uriah prophesied against Jerusalem and was killed by King Jehoiakim – yet another example of Jerusalem killing the prophets ([ref:Jer 26:20-23|Jeremiah 26:20-23]).

The image of an eagle spreading its wings over its young is the background for Jesus' picture of a hen gathering her chicks under her wings. God wanted to protect his people just as an eagle protects its young ([ref:Deut 32:11-12|Deuteronomy 32:11-12]).

The psalmist asks to be kept as the apple of the eye and hidden in the shadow of God's wings – the same image of God's care and protection that Jesus uses regarding his desire to gather Jerusalem's children ([ref:Ps 17:8|Psalms 17:8]).

The children of men seek refuge in the shadow of God's wings. The wing metaphor expresses God's protective care, the same image Jesus uses concerning his wish for Jerusalem ([ref:Ps 36:8|Psalms 36:8]).
Under his wings you will find refuge – this image of God's protection under his wings is what Jesus applies to himself when he wishes to gather Jerusalem's children ([ref:Ps 91:4|Psalms 91:4]).
Ruth sought refuge under the wings of Israel's God. The same image of God's protective wings that Jesus uses regarding his desire to protect Jerusalem ([ref:Ruth 2:12|Ruth 2:12]).
The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus voices the same lament over Jerusalem, using identical imagery about the hen and her chicks ([ref:Matt 23:37|Matthew 23:37]).

Stephen accuses the Jews: "Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? They killed those who foretold the coming of the Righteous One." This confirms Jesus' lament that Jerusalem kills the prophets ([ref:Acts 7:52|Acts 7:52]).

Paul speaks of the Jews who killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets – an echo of Jesus' words that Jerusalem kills the prophets and stones those sent to the city ([ref:1 Thess 2:15|1 Thessalonians 2:15]).
